claims.text: The 1975 record at this installation is a continuous operational log, not a report. The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log covers 7 to 19 November 1975 with timed entries naming missile sites M-1, L-3, Lima, L-6, K-1, K-4, L-1, E-1, M-8, R-3 and R-4, the Harlowton launch control facility, radar track J330, and two F-106s scrambled at 0754Z on 8 November. Its final entry is marked in the original as the last pertaining to these incidents.

claims.source: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 8 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The non-interception detail that the board's existing claim attributes to FOIA case 97-F-1677 is independently corroborated by the log's own words: '8 Nov 75 (0905Z) - From SAC CP: L-sites had fighters and objects; fighters did not get down to objects.' and '8 Nov 75 (0915Z) - From SAC CP: From four different points: Observed objects and fighters; when fighters arrived in the area, the lights went out; when fighters departed, the lights came back on; to NCOC.' Note that The Black Vault's landing page for 97-F-1677 reproduces no document text, so the log is the better citation for this claim.

Malmstrom sits on both sides of the 1967 engineering question as well as the 1975 sighting record. The 341st SMW history records that a power-switching test was conducted at Malmstrom with the Montana Power Company on 28 March 1967 at the request of OOAMA as part of the Echo Flight investigation, on the 50 kV line between the Harlowton and Glengarry substations, and that after the tests commercial power switching was ruled out as the cause.

desc: Strategic Air Command installation at Great Falls, Montana, controlling Minuteman ICBM launch facilities across a wide area of the state, and the site of two of the most heavily documented nuclear-weapons-related UFO events in the American record: the March 1967 missile-facility incident and the November 1975 overflights. The 1975 records, released by the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense under FOIA case 97-F-1677, describe numerous unidentified craft over the base and its missile fields and record that F-106 interceptors were unable to acquire them. Six years earlier the Air Force had publicly closed Project Blue Book on the finding that no UFO had ever given any indication of threat to national security. Malmstrom is where that finding meets the Air Force's own operational message traffic.
